LLM_description:
Situation:
Supply Depot Bravo and Forward Logistics Hub Delta are supporting operations in a contested corridor with limited maneuver windows and intermittent route denial. The 3rd Infantry Battalion at FOB Ridge and the 1st Armored Company at COP Hammer are executing offensive and holding tasks while maintaining readiness for rapid repositioning. Lines of communication run along MSR Falcon (longer, more secure) and MSR Viper (shorter, exposed to indirect fire and IED activity). Weather, civilian traffic, and periodic route clearance operations constrain convoy movement. Rotary-wing lift is prioritized for casualty evacuation and is not available for resupply; ground convoys are the primary mode.

Mission:
Sustain the supported units with required classes of supply over the planning horizon while minimizing total operational cost, including transport costs, shortage penalties, vehicle deployment costs, and fixed route security risk costs.

Execution/Concept:
- Prioritize delivery to maintain combat power and essential services at the supported positions, using available depot stocks without exceeding per-day throughput at each depot.
- Coordinate movements by supply type and destination; cargo volumes per item type are accounted for when loading vehicles. Vehicle loads must not exceed per-vehicle capacity, and total vehicles deployed per day must remain within fleet availability.
- Convoys will use designated depot-to-unit routes. A route can only carry vehicles on a day if it is activated. Activating any depot-to-unit route on a given day incurs a fixed Risk Cost representing security overhead (escort teams, EOD/route clearance, ISR coverage), regardless of the number of vehicles dispatched on that route.
- Transport costs apply to the quantities moved from each depot to each unit per supply type and day. Shortfalls are allowed only if operationally necessary; any unmet demand is captured as slack and penalized via shortage penalties.
- Optimize the daily plan to minimize total operational cost: select which routes to activate, assign vehicles within fleet limits, and schedule flows to meet demands while balancing transport, risk, vehicle, and shortage penalty costs.
- Deconflict movements with route clearance, patrol schedules, and fire support plans. Employ staggered departures, redundant communications, and contingency reroutes to mitigate ambush risk and chokepoints.
- Report deviations and reoptimize as conditions change (route interdictions, depot replenishment, demand shifts).
